M14.intro: Statutory compliance and tax covers provident fund (PF), ESI, professional tax (PT), labour welfare fund (LWF), income tax deducted at source (TDS) and gratuity. Payroll calculates them from rule versions that PeopleOS maintains. You record your registrations, choose which statutes apply at each establishment, look after declarations and proofs, and produce returns, challans and registers.
M14.why: Wrong registrations, profiles or employee details give wrong deductions, returns that fail validation and late or short payments. Payroll cannot be finalised while a rule version your establishments need is unverified.
M14.who: Tenant Super Admin (everything). Tenant HR Admin (all payroll and compliance permissions). Payroll Admin (payroll, statutory overrides, compliance view and compliance reports, but not registrations, returns or TDS proofs unless given those permissions). Auditor (view only). Employees declare their own investments and send proofs (payroll.payslip).
M14.where: People › Pay › Compliance control room, Compliance rules, Rule verification, Regulatory notices, Statutory registrations, Statutory profiles, TDS deductor profiles, PF options (VPF), Statutory overrides, Tax declarations, Declare investments, TDS investment proofs, Perquisites and other income, EPF returns (ECR), ESI returns, Professional tax returns, LWF returns, Challans, TDS statements (Form 138), TDS certificates (Form 130), Compliance reports. Income tax settings: Admin › Setup › Payroll (group Income tax).
objectives: Set up registrations and statutory profiles per establishment and read the compliance control room to see what blocks payroll and returns.
Run the income tax cycle: declaration, proof submission, verification and their effect on monthly TDS.
Produce each month's EPF, ESI, PT and LWF returns and challans, the quarterly Form 138 statement, Form 130 certificates and the compliance report pack.

warnings.title: Unverified rules stop payroll
warnings.headline: While a rule version your establishments need is not Verified, its payroll lines raise blocking exceptions.
warnings.body: With enforcement ON (always in live use), a line calculated from a Draft or In review version, or one under an open notice, is a blocking exception. The run cannot be validated or finalised, so no return can be built for that month.
points: Example organisation, November 2026: all 5 entries show 'is review, not verified against an official source' and 'affected by a regulatory change'.
Message on validate: 'N employee(s) have blocking exceptions. Fix the inputs and recalculate.'
Statutory overrides do not remove these exceptions.
warnings.todo: Check Rules this tenant needs in the control room and ask PeopleOS support for the verification of each red rule.

warnings.title: Software, not legal advice
warnings.headline: PeopleOS applies rule versions; it does not confirm that you are compliant.
warnings.body: Rates, ceilings and slabs are parameters of rule versions maintained by PeopleOS. A rule is 'Verified against an official source' only after PeopleOS checks official evidence. Exporting a file is not filing; PeopleOS never files or pays.
points: Software ready ≠ statutory rules verified ≠ production payroll ready ≠ return filed.
Proposed versions appear only in compliance reports, labelled provisional.
Filing and payment happen on the authorities' portals and at the bank.
warnings.todo: Have your compliance adviser confirm applicability, registrations and amounts.

warnings.headline: One person cannot take a return from generation to filing.
warnings.body: The person who generates a return cannot approve it. The filer must be neither generator nor approver. The approver cannot record its challan payment, and the recorder of a challan cannot verify it.
points: Plan at least three people with compliance.returns permissions.

Registrations and proofs: the recorder or submitter cannot verify.

warnings.body: Checks include finalised payroll, verified legal entity, establishment and registration, employees explicitly assigned, verified rules with evidence, a verified export layout, reconciliation, no blocking issues, approval by someone else and an intact audit chain.

troubleshooting: Payroll exception: '… is review, not verified against an official source'
The rule version is Draft or In review and enforcement is on.
Nothing to fix on your side; ask PeopleOS support. Check status in Compliance rules.
Payroll exception: '… affected by a regulatory change from …'
An open regulatory notice covers that rule version on that date.
Read Regulatory notices › Details; PeopleOS resolves it with a new version.
'Professional tax applies but no state is known for the employee's establishment.'
The establishment has no state, or the employee has no establishment.
Add the state (Organisation › Structure › Establishments) and the employee's establishment assignment; recalculate.
'PAN not on file; tax deducted at the higher rate (s.206AA).'
The employee has no PAN in statutory details.
Employee profile › More › Edit statutory details: enter the PAN; recalculate the run.
TDS ignores a new declaration
The run was calculated before the declaration was saved.
Recalculate the run.
'An overlapping … profile already exists for this establishment; close it first.'
Two profiles of one statute would overlap.
Close the old profile on the day before the new one starts.
'This would change whether … applied in …, whose payroll is approved or finalised…'
The change affects a month already approved or finalised.
Make it effective after that month, or ask PeopleOS support.
'This registration number is already active for another establishment.'
The number is recorded elsewhere.
Check the other establishment; close or correct that registration first.
'A registration cannot be verified by the person who recorded it.'
Separation of duties.
Ask a colleague with compliance.registrations.manage to verify.
'No finalized payroll for …; statutory returns are built from finalized payroll only.'
The month's payroll is not finalised.
Finalise payroll (M13), then generate.
Return validation: 'no UAN on file' or 'no ESI insurance (IP) number on file'
Identifier missing on the employee.
Add the UAN or ESIC number (employee profile › More › Edit statutory details); regenerate.
'Separation of duties: the person who generated a return cannot approve it.'
You generated it.
Another user with compliance.returns.approve approves.
Export refused: 'production gate blocks'
One or more gate checks fail.
See the PRODUCTION GATE tooltip; fix your items, ask PeopleOS about rules and layouts.
'Form No. 130 is prepared only from a verified annual ledger…'
Not all four Form 138 statements are acknowledged or they no longer match.
Record acknowledgements; click Verify annual ledger, then Prepare Form 130.
'You cannot override your own statutory amounts.'
Overrides on your own pay are not allowed.
Ask another user with payroll.override.

A state, type or appropriate government is missing on an establishment.
Follow WHAT TO DO for each row; regenerate.
checklist: Rules this tenant needs, Missing registrations and open notices checked.

By someone other than the generator.

M15.intro: Expense and travel covers business spending. Employees request trips and advances, file expenses, put them in expense reports for approval, and are repaid outside payroll or with payroll. As administrator you set up the categories, limits and forms, and you watch approvals, payments and the recovery of advances.
M15.why: Without categories and an expense policy nobody can claim at all. Without the payment and recovery steps, approved money is never repaid, advances are never settled, and finance, payroll and the employees' balances drift apart.
M15.who: Expense Admin (every expense permission: masters, decisions, payments). Tenant HR Admin and Tenant Super Admin (everything). Payroll Admin (view and pay). HR Manager (view and approve). Manager (claim, and approve for the team). Employee (claim own). Auditor (view). The travel desk needs expense.travel_desk. Salary reimbursement claims and bills need payroll.manage (Payroll Admin).
M15.where: People › Pay › Expense desk, Expense categories, Expense groups, Location groups, Tax, Expense and travel forms, Travel requests, Expense advances, Dispense advances, Expense receipts, Expense reports, Pay expenses, Advance recovery, Reimbursement claims, Reimbursement bills. Settings: Admin › Setup (module Expense). Expense policies: Workflows › Policies.
objectives: Set up expense groups, categories with limits, location groups, tax heads and the expense and travel forms.
Follow a claim from travel request and advance through expense report approval to payment outside payroll or with payroll.
Reconcile what is owed each month: pay approved reports, dispense advances and recover what employees still owe.
depends_on: M06 Workflows and policies: a published Expense policy decides which categories each employee can claim; an Expense advance policy decides who may borrow
M02 My work and approvals: approvers decide expense reports, advances and trips on the Approvals page
M13 Payroll: Pay with payroll, advance payouts and advance recoveries are paid in a payroll month and settled when that run is finalized
M12 Compensation and salary structures: reimbursement claims and bills need reimbursement salary components (paid on claim, or paid every month)
M05 Users, access and integrations: expenses in another currency need an exchange rate on or before the expense date (Exchange rates)
M04 Masters and configuration: extra fields on the expense and travel forms are custom fields; expense settings live in Admin › Setup
M20 Helpdesk: legs the company books are raised to the travel desk as helpdesk requests
M09 Exit and alumni: unpaid approved reports and outstanding advances are carried into the full and final settlement

procedures.title: Prepare the expense masters
procedures.before: Agree with finance which expenses you reimburse and any place-wise limits.
steps: Open People › Pay › Expense groups. Keep the five starter groups or click Add expense group.
Open Location groups, click Add location group, name it (for example Tier 1), add states and cities, save.
Open Tax. Click Add the standard tax types if heads are missing; leave Usual rate (%) blank unless finance asks.
Open Admin › Setup, module Expense: year start month, expiry, submission windows, exceptional expenses, payment step.
procedures.result: Groups, location groups and tax heads ready for categories.

procedures.title: Create an expense category with a daily limit
procedures.before: Expense groups and (if needed) location groups exist.
steps: Open Expense categories and click Add expense category.
Choose Amount, enter Expense category name, Expense group and Expense code.
Choose type Amount. In Limits enter Specify limit amount and Limit time period Daily; add rows per location group if needed.
Set Receipt required and Min expense limit for receipt; leave Reimbursable on unless the company pays directly.
Answer the eligibility questions; add a declaration if finance wants one.
Review and create. A refusal message explains which rule to fix.
procedures.result: An active category. In the example organisation, Food and meals has a 1,500.00 daily limit.

procedures.title: Let employees claim: publish an expense policy
procedures.before: Categories exist.
steps: Open Workflows › Policies and add a policy of the Expense policy type.
In Expense categories add each category; overrides left blank use the category's own rules.
Under Limit across all categories answer the question; give Amount and Frequency if Yes.
Set who the policy applies to and publish it with an effective date.
Add an Expense advance policy: largest advance, payout By bank or With the next payroll, settle and recovery days.
procedures.result: Employees covered by the policy see its categories when they add an expense.

procedures.title: Make Invoice number mandatory on amount expenses
procedures.before: None.
steps: Open Expense and travel forms. Step 1 Expense form lists each field.
For Invoice number tick Amount under Visible on and under Mandatory on.
Click Next; adjust the travel fields if needed.
On Review give the Reason for change and click Save forms.
procedures.result: New and changed amount expenses are refused until an invoice number is given.

procedures.title: Request travel for an employee and record a company booking
procedures.before: A travel-linked category in the employee's policy; you hold expense.approve; a travel desk for company bookings.
steps: Open Travel requests and click Request travel for an employee; choose the employee.
Enter Purpose, Starts on and Ends on.
Under Journeys and stays add each journey or stay: Travel category, mode, places, dates and who books it.
Fill the travel details; enter an advance amount if the trip needs one.
Another approver decides it (you cannot decide your own). On approval company legs go to the travel desk.
The travel desk opens the trip, and under Journeys and stays clicks Record booking with the reference and cost.
procedures.result: An approved trip, Approved · booked once every company booking is recorded.

procedures.title: Approve and dispense an advance
procedures.before: The employee has an Expense advance policy that allows requests.
steps: Open Expense advances, Views › Waiting for approval.
Click Approve and keep or lower the amount, or Reject with a note.
Finance pays the employee by bank transfer or cash.
Open Dispense advances, tab To dispense, click Dispense; enter Payment reference and Paid on.
Open the advance: Settle by and, for payroll recovery, Recovered through payroll from are set.
procedures.result: A dispensed advance with an outstanding amount and a settle-by date.

procedures.title: File expenses and a report for an employee
procedures.before: The employee's expense policy covers the categories; you hold expense.approve.
steps: Open Expense receipts, click Add expense for an employee, choose the employee, date and category.
Enter amount (or distance), the form fields, attach the receipt, save. Note any capped amount in the message.
Open Expense reports, click New report for an employee, choose the employee and tick the expenses.
In step Submit switch on Submit it for approval now, or leave it as a draft for the employee.
procedures.result: A submitted report (EXR-…) split into approval parts and sent to the employee's approvers.

procedures.title: Approve a report line by line, or return it
procedures.before: A submitted report of someone in your scope (never your own).
steps: Open Expense reports, Views › Waiting for approval, and View the report.
On Expenses look at Claimable and Checks; open a receipt to see matches and files.
On Approvals click Approve; for each expense keep the claimable amount, lower it, or enter 0 to reject it.
Click Return to employee and say what to change; the employee edits and submits again.
Click Reject and give the reason.
procedures.result: When every part is decided the report is Approved, Partly approved or Rejected and Net payable is worked out.

procedures.title: Pay approved expenses outside payroll
procedures.before: Finance has paid the employee from a company bank account.
steps: Open Pay expenses, tab To pay.
Find the report (for example EXR-2026-00002, 1,630.00 in the example organisation).
Click Record payment. Step How it was paid: mode and paying account. Step Reference: reference, Paid on, note.
Tick several rows and use Record one payment for the selected.
The report moves to the Paid tab as Paid outside payroll.
procedures.result: The report is Paid and the employee is told (when payment is shown to employees).

procedures.title: Pay expenses with payroll
procedures.before: The payroll month is open and not finalized.
steps: On Pay expenses, tab To pay, click Pay with payroll; choose a Pay month or leave it blank for the next payroll.
When the run is calculated, the employee gets one Expense reimbursement line, non-taxable, outside gross.
Finalize the payroll run as usual.
The report shows Paid with payroll on the Paid tab, with the payroll as reference.
procedures.result: Expenses repaid in salary without an outside payment.

procedures.title: Recover an outstanding advance
procedures.before: A dispensed advance with money outstanding.
steps: Open Advance recovery, tab Unrecovered; use Views › Settle-by date passed.
Click Recover through payroll, choose the Salary month and Recovery amount, then Confirm.
Click Record recovery outside payroll: Recovery mode, amount, reference and Received on.
Click Ledger to see every movement; the employee moves to Recovered once nothing is owed.
procedures.result: The outstanding amount is recovered and the advance becomes Recovered or Settled.

procedures.title: Claim a salary reimbursement for an employee
procedures.before: A reimbursement component paid on claim with a credited balance; you hold payroll.manage.
steps: Open Reimbursement claims and click Claim for an employee; choose the employee.
Choose the Reimbursement (see Available to claim), date, amount, description, bills and files.
Check who approves it and submit; someone else decides it.
Once approved, the next payroll pays it non-taxable; it becomes Paid when the run is finalized.
procedures.result: An approved claim paid with payroll.

calculations.title: Net payable of an approved report
calculations.intro: What the employee is still owed after the report is decided. Company-paid lines are approved but never repaid.
explain: Net payable = reimbursable approved − dispensed advances settled (oldest first, up to the reimbursable amount).
Figures from the example organisation; no advance is outstanding there.
Expense reports (NET PAYABLE) and Pay expenses (TO PAY).

calculations.title: Report with an advance to settle (illustrative)
calculations.intro: If the employee had 1,000.00 outstanding on a dispensed advance, approving the same report settles it first.
lines: Advance outstanding, settled against the report
explain: Settled = the smaller of the advance outstanding and what the report repays; the advance becomes Settled when nothing is left.
Illustrative: the advance amount is invented.
Report: Advances settled; advance ledger: Settled against expense report.

calculations.title: A claim over the daily limit is capped
calculations.intro: With exceptional expenses switched off (as in the example organisation), the claimable amount stops at what is left of the limit.
explain: Claimable = the smaller of the amount and what is left (limit − claimed in the period, and the policy's overall limit).
Limit and first receipt from the example organisation; the 900.00 receipt is illustrative.
Expense receipts: CLAIMABLE and the Over the limit check.

calculations.title: Mileage amount (illustrative)
calculations.intro: A mileage category pays the distance at its rate per km. The example organisation has no mileage category; the figures are invented.
explain: Amount = distance × rate per km; with an odometer, distance = end reading − start reading.
A km limit is turned into money as km left × rate per km.
Expense receipts: AMOUNT shows km and amount.

calculations.title: Settle-by and payroll recovery dates (illustrative)
calculations.intro: Dates set when an advance is dispensed under a policy that recovers through payroll, using the policy defaults.
lines: Recover after the settle-by date (policy default)
explain: Settle by = payment date (or trip end, if later) + settle-within days; recovery from = settle by + recovery days.
Illustrative dates; 30 and 15 days are the defaults when the policy leaves them blank.
Advance: Settle by, Recovered through payroll from; Advance recovery: AUTOMATIC RECOVERY.

calculations.title: Available to claim on a reimbursement (illustrative)
calculations.intro: A pay-on-claim reimbursement builds a balance each finalized payroll; claims draw it down.
lines: Claims pending or approved and not yet paid
explain: Available = ledger balance for the year − payable amount of claims waiting.
Illustrative figures; the example organisation has no claims.
Claim form hint: Available to claim.

warnings.title: No policy, no claims
warnings.headline: Employees can claim only categories in their published expense policy.
warnings.body: A category on its own does nothing. Without an Expense policy the employee sees no categories and filing is refused; without an Expense advance policy advance requests are refused.
points: Message: No expense policy applies to you on …
Message: Expense advance policy needs to be configured to enable employee to request advance for work related expenses.
The example organisation has an expense policy but no advance policy.
warnings.todo: Publish both policies under Workflows › Policies before go-live.

warnings.title: PeopleOS records payments; it does not pay
warnings.headline: Record payment and Dispense only record a payment made outside PeopleOS.
warnings.body: Pay the employee through your bank first, then record the reference and date. Only Pay with payroll and payroll advance payouts move money through salary.
points: Record the bank reference exactly as in the bank statement.
Reconcile the Paid tab with the bank each month.
warnings.todo: Agree with finance who records payments and when.

warnings.title: Nothing is paid twice
warnings.headline: Once a payroll run carries a report or advance, it cannot be paid outside payroll.
warnings.body: A report scheduled for payroll is marked Paid only when that run is finalized. While a run being prepared carries it, Record payment, Change pay month and Take off payroll are refused.
points: Finalize the run, or remove the item before calculating.
A month finalized without the item shows as missed: change or cancel the schedule.
warnings.todo: Decide outside payment or payroll before the payroll is calculated.

warnings.title: Type and code are permanent
warnings.headline: A category's Expense type and Expense code cannot change after creation.
warnings.body: To move from amount to mileage, add a new category and set the old one Inactive. Categories are never deleted, so earlier claims keep their category.

warnings.title: Over the limit is capped by default
warnings.headline: With exceptional expenses off, a claim above the limit is cut to what is left.
warnings.body: The receipt keeps the full amount, the Over the limit check and the capped Claimable amount. To let employees file the excess as an exceptional expense, switch on exceptional expenses in Setup and allow it on the category.
points: Exceptional expenses always get their own approval part.

warnings.title: Workflow approval approves in full
warnings.headline: A workflow that approves a report part approves each line at its claimable amount.
warnings.body: To approve less than claimed, or reject single lines, an approver decides the part on the report's Approvals tab instead.

warnings.title: Two kinds of reimbursement
warnings.headline: Business expenses and salary reimbursement claims are different processes.
warnings.body: Expense reports cover business spending under the expense policy (expense permissions). Reimbursement claims draw on a reimbursement salary component balance and need payroll.manage. Do not claim the same bill in both.

checklist: Clear everything under Needs a look.
Expense reports › Waiting for approval; travel and advance requests waiting.
Expense receipts › Suspected duplicates and Over the limit before approval.
Pay expenses › To pay: record outside payments or Pay with payroll before the payroll cut-off.
Confirm scheduled reports show Paid with payroll on the Paid tab.
Dispense advances › To dispense: record every payout made by finance.
Advance recovery › Settle-by date passed and Recovery month missed.
Run Expense payment register and Outstanding expense advance; match references to the bank statement.
Reimbursement claims › Approved, to be paid; record bills for monthly reimbursements.
Check open reports and outstanding advances before the full and final settlement.
summary: Categories, location groups and tax heads set the rules; an expense policy decides who may claim what.
Expenses go into reports; reports split into approval parts and are approved line by line, returned or rejected.
Net payable = reimbursable approved minus advances settled; pay it outside payroll or with payroll.
PeopleOS records outside payments; payroll items are settled only when the run is finalized, never twice.
Advances: approve, dispense, then settle with reports, refunds, payroll recovery or write-off.
Salary reimbursement claims and bills are payroll processes, separate from business expenses.
